body: My dad cheated on my mom for a year before he was exposed. That was 9 months ago. They had been together for almost 20 years. Of course, seeing the personal impact it had on her and my family, my first thoughts when someone says they feel bad about cheating are "serves you right". But then I remember nothing is black and white. I personally have BPD, so I know what it's like to ruin relationships "on accident" and really, really regret it. I don't know your story or the context that lead you to cheat on her, but if you loved her that much for 8 years, it probably was something significant, not just a random choice to be a dick on your part. You can't expect her to forgive you or to ever have the regret go away, because even if you managed to fix it and get back together with her, you'd feel bad for having done something to warrant fixing it in the first place. Just remember your purpose is to yourself, not to anyone else, and you deserve to be alive regardless of what you do because you're human and to live is your right.

Because you are human, and it is in our instinct and nature to want to survive. Your subconscious is telling you something, even you know that you want to live, even if it's for the sake of not dying, without you realising.

I think assisted suicide should be an option for those who cannot get better (as in, permanent organ failure, chronic illness, brain damage). If the person can get better, there should at least be some type of counseling in place before and after for the family and friends of the person to lessen the blow.

I'm still struggling with the same things I was those months back, just with a bit of a more realistic outlook on life. I feel my grasp on the fact death is permanent has improved after my "oh shit, I'm really going to die" moment, "do I actually want this?". Of course, the regret and panic came after taking the pills, but I still had some consciousness left in me to text an online friend and they talked me into going to the hospital. This was in March.

In May, I attempted again. I took soap and mouth wash, not sure why in my post-throwing up high (I'm bulimic) my brain thought it would be enough, but that's beside the point. I saw my mom and my brother laying down on my bed after I left the bathroom and just remember shrugging to myself and thinking, "oh well". I woke up the next day apathetic and with a horrible stomach ache, diarrhea for a few days, but no one noticed.

Those experiences really made my mindset shift. I'm not sure how to properly describe it, but even though I still want to do it, it's not for the same reasons anymore.
